start.speaker: saltmere_marrow
start.text: The clerk shows you through without being asked. Ines Marrow does not look up from her ledger until she has finished a line, and then she does, and her face is kind in a terrifying way. 'You have been asking after Osk Dray. In my town, that is a thing one asks me first.' She gestures at a chair. 'Tea? It is real. I am told that is rare.'

choices.text: [Insight] Read what she actually wants from you.
Take the tea. 'I need Osk's strongroom. I can be useful to you.'
[Persuasion] 'Give me the key, and you get the buyer's name.'
Decline the tea and leave. Voss will have a better offer.

reads.speaker: saltmere_marrow
reads.text: She wants Osk back, not dead, back: loyal, remorseful, and in her ledger. She wants to know who bought what he sold, and she is a little afraid of the answer. 'You have an interesting face,' says Marrow, and you realise you have been caught reading her. She is not offended. 'Then you know what I need. Bring me the buyer's name, and the strongroom key is yours.'

tea.speaker: saltmere_marrow
tea.text: 'Useful.' She tastes the word. 'Osk Dray sold something that was not his to sell, to a person I would rather not name in this room. I want the thing returned, and I want that person's name. In exchange: the Syndicate's goodwill, and the key to a door that is otherwise very difficult.' She slides an iron key across the desk. 'Do we have an arrangement?'

choices.text: [Deception] Agree, and plan to double-cross her.

little_bird.speaker: saltmere_marrow
little_bird.text: Marrow's pen stops. Sable steps out of your shadow with their hands in their pockets, looking everywhere but at her. 'Hello, Ines.' 'Little bird.' It is almost gentle. 'You always did choose your friends carefully.' She turns to you. 'Take the key. I will not pretend I don't want something back, but I will not have it said I made Sable's friend beg.'

persuaded.speaker: saltmere_marrow
persuaded.text: 'The buyer's name.' She sits back. For a moment you see the arithmetic in her eyes, the cost of the favour set against the cost of ignorance. 'Very well. A fair trade, honestly offered.' The key slides across the desk. 'Do not make me regret my manners.'

refused.speaker: saltmere_marrow
refused.text: 'No.' It is perfectly pleasant. 'You have not yet earned the door. Come back with a favour, or a better reason, or a different face.' She returns to her ledger. The clerk's smile widens as he holds the door.

respect.speaker: saltmere_marrow
respect.text: Her pen does not stop, but the tip rests very lightly on the page. 'Forty years,' she says, 'and I have been spoken to like that perhaps twice. I find I do not mind.' The key comes out of her sleeve. 'Do try not to disappoint me.'

enforcers.speaker: saltmere_marrow
enforcers.text: 'Oh, my dear,' says Marrow, with real regret. She does not look up. Two grey-coated figures step out from behind the screens. 'I did hope you'd be sensible.'

caught.speaker: saltmere_marrow
caught.text: She smiles, pleasantly. 'Mm. Of course.' The key is still in your hand, but something in the air has changed. 'You will find that I am rarely deceived, and never twice.' She goes back to her ledger.

effects.message: You leave with the key, and the distinct impression that you are being watched.

walk.speaker: saltmere_marrow
walk.text: 'Of course.' She does not rise. 'Voss is a good woman and an exhausted one. Give her my regards. Tell her the offer stands, in the unlikely event she has anything to offer.' The clerk holds the door and smiles his alarming smile.

key.speaker: saltmere_marrow
key.text: 'The strongroom is behind the tide grate on the quay, or down the clerk's back stair. Osk is polite and a coward, and he keeps a bell under his desk.' She looks down at her ledger. 'Bring me what is mine, and I will remember that you were fair.' The tea has gone cold. You do not remember drinking any.
